/-! ## The general case: uniqueness proved for an *independently produced* datum over `L`

The lemmas above take the `L`-side uniqueness at `(d.baseChange L).J`, the transport of
`d`.  But the way the geometry is actually available is different: over `k̄` one produces
a datum `dL : JacobianData C_L` in its own right (that is where the symmetric-power and
birationality machinery lives), and there is no reason for `dL` to be `d.baseChange L` on
the nose.

This is exactly the place where a representing-object comparison *is* needed — so the
claim "S10 needs no comparison" must be read narrowly: it holds for the transported
datum, not for an arbitrary one.  The comparison is cheap, though, and it is already
landed: `JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` is an isomorphism of representing objects, and
transporting a `Subsingleton` of a `Hom`-set along an isomorphism of its source costs
two rewrites.  So the general case is not a new mathematical obligation, only one more
step. -/

/-- `Subsingleton` of a `Hom`-set transports along an isomorphism of the source. -/
theorem subsingleton_hom_of_iso {D : Type*} [Category D] {X X' Y : D} (e : X ≅ X')
    (h : Subsingleton (X' ⟶ Y)) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y) :=
  ⟨fun f g => by
    have hh : e.inv ≫ f = e.inv ≫ g := h.elim _ _
    have := congrArg (fun t => e.hom ≫ t) hh
    simpa using this⟩

/-- **The S10 uniqueness half, for uniqueness proved at an arbitrary `L`-datum.**

`dL : JacobianData C_L` is any datum on the base-changed curve — in particular one
produced over `k̄` by the geometry, with no relation to `d` assumed.  Uniqueness at
`dL.J` transports to `(d.baseChange L).J` through `uniqueUpToIso` (both represent
`Pic⁰_{C_L/L}`, so they are canonically isomorphic), and thence down to `k` by
faithfulness.

Together with `existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange` this covers both stagings, and
records honestly that the comparison is unavoidable in this one — cheap, but present. -/
theorem existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange_datum (d : JacobianData C)
    (dL : JacobianData ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C))
    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : C ⟶ A)
    (hex : ∃ g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g)
    (hL : Subsingleton (dL.J ⟶ (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj A)) :
    ∃! g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g :=
  existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange L d P f hex
    (subsingleton_hom_of_iso ((d.baseChange L).uniqueUpToIso dL) hL)

end JacobianData

end AlgebraicGeometry

130	theorem monObjObj_eq_ofRepresentableBy {C₁ : Type u₁} {D₁ : Type u₂}
131	    [Category.{w} C₁] [Category.{w} D₁] [CartesianMonoidalCategory C₁]
132	    [CartesianMonoidalCategory D₁] {F : C₁ ⥤ D₁} {G : D₁ ⥤ C₁} (adj : F ⊣ G)
133	    [G.Monoidal] (Y : D₁) [MonObj Y] :
134	    Functor.monObjObj (F := G) (X := Y)
135	      = MonObj.ofRepresentableBy (G.obj Y) (F.op ⋙ yonedaMonObj Y) (adj.representableBy Y) := by
136	  refine MonObj.ext _ _ ?_
137	  rw [MonObj.ofRepresentableBy_mul, eq_comm, Equiv.symm_apply_eq]
138	  change (adj.homEquiv (MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj (G.obj Y) (G.obj Y)) Y).symm
139	          (fst (G.obj Y) (G.obj Y))
140	        * (adj.homEquiv (MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj (G.obj Y) (G.obj Y)) Y).symm
141	          (snd (G.obj Y) (G.obj Y))
142	      = (adj.homEquiv (MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorObj (G.obj Y) (G.obj Y)) Y).symm
143	          (Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ G Y Y ≫ G.map μ[Y])
144	  rw [Hom.mul_def, Adjunction.homEquiv_counit, Adjunction.homEquiv_counit,
145	    Adjunction.homEquiv_counit, Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc, Adjunction.counit_naturality,
146	    ← Category.assoc (F.map (Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ G Y Y))]
147	  congr 1
148	  refine CartesianMonoidalCategory.hom_ext _ _ ?_ ?_
149	  · rw [CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift_fst, ← Functor.Monoidal.μ_fst, Functor.map_comp,
150	      Category.assoc, adj.counit_naturality, Category.assoc]
151	  · rw [CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift_snd, ← Functor.Monoidal.μ_snd, Functor.map_comp,
152	      Category.assoc, adj.counit_naturality, Category.assoc]

156	/-! ## A general lemma: `MonObj.ofRepresentableBy` transports along presheaf-of-monoid isos -/

162	open CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
163	
164	/-- **`MonObj.ofRepresentableBy` is invariant under transport of the representing datum along a
165	presheaf-of-monoids isomorphism** (the reusable half of B-6a): if `Φ : F ≅ F'` is an isomorphism of
166	presheaves of monoids whose forgetful action intertwines the universal `homEquiv`s of two
167	representability data `α`, `α'` for a common representing object `X`, then the two induced
168	`MonObj X` structures coincide.  Proved elementwise through `homEquiv`'s injectivity and the
169	component multiplicativity of `Φ.hom`, never diagram-chasing in `Mon _` (the R3 term-mode
170	discipline). -/
171	theorem monObj_ofRepresentableBy_eq_of_iso {D : Type u₁} [Category.{w} D]
172	    [CartesianMonoidalCategory D] {F F' : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ MonCat.{w}} (Φ : F ≅ F') {X : D}
173	    (α : (F ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget _).RepresentableBy X)
174	    (α' : (F' ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget _).RepresentableBy X)
175	    (h : ∀ {T : D} (g : T ⟶ X), α'.homEquiv g = Φ.hom.app (op T) (α.homEquiv g)) :
176	    MonObj.ofRepresentableBy X F α = MonObj.ofRepresentableBy X F' α' := by
177	  refine MonObj.ext _ _ ?_
178	  simp only [MonObj.ofRepresentableBy_mul, Functor.RepresentableBy.homEquiv']
179	  apply α'.homEquiv.injective
180	  rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply, h, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, map_mul, ← h, ← h]
181	
182	end OfRepTransport

199	theorem grpObjObj_baseChange_eq (d : JacobianData C) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :

206	    (Over.mapPullbackAdj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))) d.J).trans ?_
207	  exact monObj_ofRepresentableBy_eq_of_iso
208	    (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).op
209	        (yonedaMonObjIsoOfRepresentableBy d.J
210	          (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat) d.rep)
211	      ≪≫ (Functor.isoWhiskerRight (pic0Theta k L C)
212	          (forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat)).symm)

230	    letI := dL.grpObj
231	    (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk d.J) ≅ .mk dL.J :=
232	  letI := d.grpObj
233	  letI := dL.grpObj
234	  letI := (d.baseChange L).grpObj

240	        ((pic0Functor ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C) ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
241	          ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat) dL.rep
242	      IsMonHom ((d.baseChange L).uniqueUpToIso dL).hom :=
243	    isMonHom_hom_of_representableBy
244	      ((pic0Functor ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C) ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
245	        ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat)

250	        Grp (Over (Spec (.of L)))))

10	/-!
11	# S10 at the datum level: the Albanese uniqueness clause descends from `k̄` to `k`
12	
13	`Albanese/BaseFieldFaithful.lean` proves that base change along an arbitrary field
14	extension is a faithful functor on `Over (Spec k)`.  This file spends that on the
15	Wave-6 descent leaf, at the interface the frozen gate actually consumes: the Jacobian
16	datum `d : JacobianData C` and its transport `d.baseChange L`.
17	
18	The point of contact is a definitional one.  `JacobianData.baseChange`
19	(`Picard/JacobianDataBaseChange.lean:60`) is *defined* with representing object
20	
21	```
22	(d.baseChange L).J = (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj d.J
23	```
24	
25	so a morphism out of the base-changed Jacobian **is** a morphism out of the base change
26	of `d.J`, with no comparison isomorphism in between.  Faithfulness therefore applies on
27	the nose, and the uniqueness clause of `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` over `k` follows from
28	the same clause over `L`.
29	
30	## What this buys, and what it does not
31	
32	The recon (`informal/w6-albanese-port-recon.md` §3, row S10) budgeted the whole leaf as
33	"finite-level spreading + Milne-6.4 uniqueness-first Galois argument + the
34	`(Jacobian C)_{k̄} ≅` representing-object comparison", with "nothing" landed or portable.
35	Two of those three items are not needed for uniqueness:
36	
37	* **no finite-level spreading out** — faithfulness holds at `k → k̄` directly, since it
38	  needs only flatness and surjectivity of `Spec k̄ ⟶ Spec k`, neither of which sees
39	  finiteness.  §4.2's worry that the staging "at the *non-finite* extension k̄ is pinned
40	  nowhere" dissolves: there is nothing to stage;
41	* **no representing-object comparison** — `(d.baseChange L).J` is the base change of
42	  `d.J` by definition, so `uniqueUpToIso` is not in the path at all.  (A comparison
43	  *is* needed if one insists on relating `d.baseChange L` to some independently produced
44	  datum `dL` on `C_L`; `uniqueUpToIso` covers that, and `subsingleton_hom_of_descends`
45	  below is stated so the caller may route through either.)
46	
47	What remains genuinely Galois is **existence**: producing a `k`-morphism `d.J ⟶ A` from
48	a `k̄`-morphism.  Nothing here addresses it.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.subsingleton_hom_baseChange_descends` — uniqueness of
53	  morphisms out of the base-changed Jacobian descends to uniqueness over `k`.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange` — **the S10
55	  uniqueness half**: given the factorisation over `k` and uniqueness over `L`, the
56	  Albanese `∃!` holds over `k`.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.eq_of_baseChange_eq` — the raw descent of an equation
58	  between two morphisms out of the Jacobian.
59	-/

65	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

71	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
72	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	  (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
74	
75	/-- **Descent of an equation between morphisms out of the Jacobian.**  Two `k`-morphisms
76	`d.J ⟶ A` that agree after base change to `L` are equal.
77	
78	The `L`-side equation is literally an equation of morphisms
79	`(d.baseChange L).J ⟶ (baseChange k L).obj A`, because `(d.baseChange L).J` is defined as
80	`(baseChange k L).obj d.J`; no transport is involved. -/
81	theorem eq_of_baseChange_eq (d : JacobianData C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))}
82	    {g g' : d.J ⟶ A}
83	    (h : (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).map g
84	      = (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).map g') :
85	    g = g' :=
86	  eq_of_baseChange_map_eq (L := L) h
87	
88	/-- **Uniqueness descends.**  If the base-changed Jacobian has at most one morphism to
89	`A_L`, then `d.J` has at most one morphism to `A`.
90	
91	This is the shape Milne's uniqueness-first pattern needs: run the geometric argument
92	over `k̄`, where the symmetric-power and birationality machinery lives, and read the
93	conclusion off over `k`. -/
94	theorem subsingleton_hom_baseChange_descends (d : JacobianData C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))}
95	    (h : Subsingleton ((d.baseChange L).J ⟶ (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj A)) :
96	    Subsingleton (d.J ⟶ A) :=
97	  subsingleton_of_subsingleton_baseChange (L := L) h
98	
99	/-- **The S10 uniqueness half of the Albanese universal property.**
100	
101	Assembles the frozen `∃!` over `k` from:
102	
103	* `hex` — existence of *some* factorisation over `k`.  This is the Galois-cocycle half
104	  and is supplied by the caller; it is not proved here;
105	* `hL` — uniqueness of morphisms out of the base-changed Jacobian, i.e. the geometric
106	  argument run over `L = k̄`.
107	
108	No Galois group, no cocycle, no spreading out to a finite level appears in the proof:
109	the descent is `Over.pullback`-faithfulness of a flat surjective base, which is
110	insensitive to whether `k → L` is finite, separable, or algebraic. -/
111	theorem existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange (d : JacobianData C)
112	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : C ⟶ A)
113	    (hex : ∃ g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g)
114	    (hL : Subsingleton ((d.baseChange L).J ⟶ (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj A)) :
115	    ∃! g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g := by
116	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hex
117	  exact ⟨g, hg, fun _ _ => (subsingleton_hom_baseChange_descends L d hL).elim _ _⟩
118	
119	/-! ## The general case: uniqueness proved for an *independently produced* datum over `L`
120	
121	The lemmas above take the `L`-side uniqueness at `(d.baseChange L).J`, the transport of
122	`d`.  But the way the geometry is actually available is different: over `k̄` one produces
123	a datum `dL : JacobianData C_L` in its own right (that is where the symmetric-power and
124	birationality machinery lives), and there is no reason for `dL` to be `d.baseChange L` on
125	the nose.
126	
127	This is exactly the place where a representing-object comparison *is* needed — so the
128	claim "S10 needs no comparison" must be read narrowly: it holds for the transported
129	datum, not for an arbitrary one.  The comparison is cheap, though, and it is already
130	landed: `JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` is an isomorphism of representing objects, and
131	transporting a `Subsingleton` of a `Hom`-set along an isomorphism of its source costs
132	two rewrites.  So the general case is not a new mathematical obligation, only one more
133	step. -/
134	
135	/-- `Subsingleton` of a `Hom`-set transports along an isomorphism of the source. -/
136	theorem subsingleton_hom_of_iso {D : Type*} [Category D] {X X' Y : D} (e : X ≅ X')
137	    (h : Subsingleton (X' ⟶ Y)) : Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y) :=
138	  ⟨fun f g => by
139	    have hh : e.inv ≫ f = e.inv ≫ g := h.elim _ _
140	    have := congrArg (fun t => e.hom ≫ t) hh
141	    simpa using this⟩
142	
143	/-- **The S10 uniqueness half, for uniqueness proved at an arbitrary `L`-datum.**
144	
145	`dL : JacobianData C_L` is any datum on the base-changed curve — in particular one
146	produced over `k̄` by the geometry, with no relation to `d` assumed.  Uniqueness at
147	`dL.J` transports to `(d.baseChange L).J` through `uniqueUpToIso` (both represent
148	`Pic⁰_{C_L/L}`, so they are canonically isomorphic), and thence down to `k` by
149	faithfulness.
150	
151	Together with `existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange` this covers both stagings, and
152	records honestly that the comparison is unavoidable in this one — cheap, but present. -/
153	theorem existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange_datum (d : JacobianData C)
154	    (dL : JacobianData ((AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj C))
155	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : C ⟶ A)
156	    (hex : ∃ g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g)
157	    (hL : Subsingleton (dL.J ⟶ (AlgebraicGeometry.baseChange k L).obj A)) :
158	    ∃! g : d.J ⟶ A, f = d.ofCurve P ≫ g :=
159	  existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_baseChange L d P f hex
160	    (subsingleton_hom_of_iso ((d.baseChange L).uniqueUpToIso dL) hL)
161	
162	end JacobianData

[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)

-- data
/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  sorry

namespace Jacobian

/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/

-- data
/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
  sorry

/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
genus of `C`. -/
instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
  sorry

/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
  sorry

/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
  sorry

/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
  sorry

/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
  sorry

/--
The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
-/
theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
  sorry

/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
  map _ := sorry
  map_id := sorry
  map_comp := sorry

end Jacobian

/-! ## Base change of fields

Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
compatibility of the Jacobian. -/

/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
-/
noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
